title.en: Timed colored Petri net: bindings and model time

summary: Bind typed token values and advance an explicit model clock without turning animation duration into net semantics.
objective: Build a bounded timed colored Petri-net inspector where I choose a legal variable binding, fire it atomically, and advance model time only when no ready binding remains.
intent_signals: inspect token binding guards and timestamps
example_prompts: Make a small timed colored Petri net where red and blue jobs have different delays and I can inspect every enabled binding.
negative_signals: Not a plain weighted P/T net, stochastic net, time-Petri interval model, performance predictor or proof of liveness, fairness or boundedness.
not_for: No stochastic timing, transition time intervals, unbounded color domains, inhibitor/reset arcs, state-space proof or real-time wall-clock coupling.

entities.name: Typed places and tokens
entities.guidance: Blender builds stable trays, transition gates and token families with readable silhouettes; token instances show value, multiplicity and availability timestamp rather than relying on hue.

entities.name: Binding and clock inspector
entities.guidance: Three.js owns finite color sets, typed multisets, variable bindings, guards, the discrete global clock and atomic history. Show color-enabled separately from ready-at-current-time.

state_contract.model: Finite places and transitions; every place declares a finite color set. A marking maps each place to a multiset of typed tokens (value, availability timestamp). Each transition has typed input patterns, output expressions, a Boolean guard and nonnegative integer output delays. A binding is color-enabled when its substituted input multiset is available and its guard is true; it is ready at model time tau only when every consumed timed token has timestamp <= tau. Firing at tau atomically consumes the bound inputs and creates outputs timestamped tau+delay. Stay at tau while a ready binding exists; when none exists, advance only to the least later time at which a color-enabled binding becomes ready. A declared tie policy selects among simultaneous ready bindings without claiming fairness.
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns the typed model, clock and history. Blender-authored meshes are stable presentation parts; tween duration never advances the model clock.
actions: Select a transition and inspect all finite legal bindings with guard and readiness reasons.
Fire one chosen ready binding atomically, or reject the attempt without partial token movement.
Advance to the next event time only when no binding is ready; step back by restoring an exact snapshot.
Load a two-color service preset in which output delay depends on the bound job color.

invariants: Every token value belongs to its place color set; ill-typed arc expressions, negative delays and out-of-domain bindings are errors that commit no state.
A future-stamped token may satisfy the color/multiset pattern but cannot be consumed before its timestamp.
Firing is one marking update at tau: there is no semantic intermediate state with inputs removed and outputs not yet created.
Clock advance cannot skip a ready binding at the current time and cannot use render-frame delta as model time.
motion_guidance: Step commits one discrete semantic action; pause freezes playback without changing committed state. Reset cancels pending animation and restores the complete preset, including clock, history, selection and error state.
Use a static before/after view and readable tables for reduced motion. Camera movement and token/message travel only explain a committed transition.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive, stable parts and materials for the chosen metaphor; Three.js binds those parts to model IDs and derives every label, highlight and transform from semantic state. Color is reinforced with text, shape or pattern.
The layout may be sculptural, planar or spatial, provided ordering, identity and invalid states remain unambiguous.
known_limits: Finite declared colors and nonnegative integer model time only; no stochastic distributions, transition intervals, hierarchy, state-space analysis or fairness guarantee.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, solver, allocator, TLS stack, browser, renderer or interactive artifact was run.

physical_contract.scope: Typed tokens and model time are abstract state; mesh motion and collisions have no causal role.

object_craft.structure: Use keyed token silhouettes that visibly fit their declared place trays; duplicate tokens stack or fan while retaining multiplicity badges. Put the model-time dial beside the binding table.
object_craft.material: Assign restrained color families plus engraved value/type glyphs and timestamp tabs; reserve emission for the currently selected ready binding.

claims.statement: Colored Petri nets use typed token values and multisets; variables in arc inscriptions form transition bindings, and a Boolean guard permits only bindings that evaluate true.
claims.scope: The finite CPN subset declared by this recipe; not plain anonymous-token P/T-net semantics.

source_refs.locator: Slides 22–29 and 42: multisets, typed arc variables, binding elements and Boolean guards

claims.statement: In the documented timed CP-net semantics, token timestamps state their earliest usable model time; a binding must be color-enabled and ready, occurrences are instantaneous, output delays timestamp produced tokens, and the global clock advances when no binding can execute at the current time.
claims.scope: CPN Tools-style timestamp semantics with a discrete clock and nonnegative output delays; not general time-Petri intervals.

source_refs.locator: PDF pages 2–4 (PDF indices 1–3): global clock, readiness, instantaneous occurrence, clock advance and @+ output delay
